evidence.note: Fourth reachable plain Error: same quantity group/role/length/count/points, but different size. quantityLineId at 201 omits size; memberGroupKey uses Story.name at project.ts:194, not Story.id.

Counterexample imports two stories with equal names, distinct IDs, registered C1 sections selected by exact storyLabel a/b, and D10/D13 hoops. All six placements accepted; JSON validation passes. run begins undefined; girderRun executes inside try at 206. Non-MemberUnsupportedError is rethrown at 218. The handled catch enumerates run?.members ?? [member] at 220-221 and appends each at 237. If girderRun throws before assignment, only the current member is available; this is not a claim that current mixed-section errors are handled.
Existing comment: 同一断面であることを連続の条件にする。 The actual predicate is candidate.sectionId === member.sectionId at 1273; both adjacency scans use slabAt at 1284/1289.

Placement loop checks only missing section 162, multiple sections 166, role mismatch 171 and grid bounds 175. It never compares neighboring sectionId values before appending members at 180. drawing-set/apply.ts:29 delegates to this function.

Unsupported lookup returns at 1404 before girderRun at 1484 and runSupportSections at 1498. The helper is defined earlier (1363) and its calls 1373/1375 are textually earlier, but execute only through the later call. Neither is wrapped in try. This is runtime control-flow ordering, not a claim that the helper definition is inside selectedMemberView.
useTakeoff supplies unsupportedMembers; IDs flow to buildingLayout at 1585-1592 and the list to selectedMemberView at 1599-1605.
Concrete loop ends at 296. It uses gridPoint and section dimensions for columns/girders; no girderSpan or beamDepthAbove call. It DOES call slabBay at 220 and wallSpan at 250.
Rebar loop skips unsupported IDs at 303 before girderSpan at 341.

claims.limitation: This claim does not prove every concrete box is safe: slabBay/wallSpan can throw MemberUnsupportedError outside a catch in the concrete loop. Such typed failures are not a fourth plain Error under B1. The phase gate is already refuted by the concrete B1 counterexample.

evidence.note: Object.keys(ja).filter((key) => !(key in ko)) equals []; this is ja subset of ko, not equality.
Record<UnsupportedReason,true> lists every union member. Extending the union makes this object lack a required property during TypeScript checking (Vitest execution alone is not a type check).
Loops cover both takeoff/viewer and reason/plan in ja/ko. Lines 41-42 use not.toBe(key), so a missing ja translation returns the key and fails the ja assertion.
Lookup is resources[locale][key] ?? resources.ja[key] ?? key; ko fallback by itself does not prove a ko entry. The subset assertion supplies that proof.

findSection requires a broken section reference to fail. Import selects existing section object and stores its id at apply.ts:170/186; applyElevation preserves sections. Applies also to findSection calls before try and before viewer unsupported checks.

Pre-try section/story lookups and kind guards 102/134/171/198, plus catch helpers 224/229/234, cannot fail from accepted role-matched imports with valid initial references. Rethrows 120/153/185/218 propagate plain errors, not separate origins.

Run cannot be empty after successful girderRun: current member survives filter and members slice contains it. Owner lookup at 1487 uses members[0].id. slabRun seeds [member] at project.ts:1282, so own-run lookup 1433 cannot fail. Kind/reference guards follow import invariants.
